abstract: Upon acute stress, cells rapidly engage autophagy to preserve integrity and adapt. This is tightly coupled to membrane remodeling, notably mobilization and reorganization of endosomal compartments supporting autophagosome formation. Here, we uncover a stress-specific partnership between the small GTPases RAB11 and RAB30 that orchestrates endosomal trafficking during response to physiological stress. TurboID-based proximity labeling of RAB11A combined with mass spectrometry identifies RAB30, a Golgi-localized protein, as a critical stress-specific partner. Upon stress, RAB30 relocalizes to RAB11-positive endosomes and is required for autophagic response and cell survival. Using stress conditions-starvation, shear stress, and osmotic stress-we show that RAB11 and RAB30 are indispensable for cell survival and autophagy, extending RAB11's role beyond recycling to the cell surface. Under shear and nutritional stress, RAB11 compartments undergo morphodynamic remodeling governed by local PI3P/PI4P turnover essential for RAB30 mobilization. Our findings highlight a phosphoinositide-driven RAB11-RAB30 axis integrating membrane trafficking and autophagy under stress, revealing a dedicated endosomal circuit for adaptive membrane supply.

summary: RAB11 and RAB30 cooperate on endosomes under starvation, shear and osmotic stress, using phosphoinositide turnover to drive autophagy and cell survival.
title: RAB11-RAB30 partnership drives stress-induced endosomal remodeling via a phosphoinositide switch.
